newsitem.title: USA: KCBT WHEAT ENDS LOWER IN SYMPATHY WITH CORN, SOY.
newsitem.headline: KCBT WHEAT ENDS LOWER IN SYMPATHY WITH CORN, SOY.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled lower in quiet dealings on spillover pressure from CBOT corn and soybeans, traders said.
"Wheat was influenced by the fall crops," a KCBT trader said.

Corn and beans opened sharply lower after beneficial rains fell over the weekend in dry growing areas of Illinois and Indiana. Meteorologists said more rain was forecast to hit the area through Tuesday.
KCBT wheat settled one to four cents lower, with September down four cents at $3.76 a bushel.
KCBT traders said they had seen some position-evening ahead of the scheduled Tuesday release of USDA's August crop report.
"The report kept a lot of people on the sidelines, and those who were in were pretty much just squaring their positions out," another trader said.

Traders said FIMAT Futures sold 1.1 million bushels each of September and December wheat. E. D. and F. Man International bull-spread one million Sept/Dec at 14 cents per bushel and 1.2 million Sept/March at 21-1/2 to 22-1/2 cents.
KCBT estimated Monday's wheat futures volume at 28.205 million bushels, against 31.67 million Friday
